solutions.check: 30 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 29 answers the paper printed; printed-crossing fills: 19-down

clue.text: One boy returns after another this term

indicators.note: after places the turned-round boy behind the other boy

parts.note: Michael is another boy's name

indicators.note: returns means this boy's name comes back the other way

parts.note: Sam is a boy's name

explanation.surface: One lad comes back to school after another has arrived for the new term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns SAM into MAS, which follows MICHAEL. In Britain Michaelmas is also the name of the autumn term at universities and some schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumn term at Oxford, Cambridge and many schools takes its name from the feast of St Michael on 29 September.

clue.text: Drink for an ancient lawmaker, say

indicators.note: say signals that the lawmaker's name is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a Mede, one of the ancient people whose 'law of the Medes and Persians' could not be altered

explanation.surface: A toast to a lawgiver of old.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'law of the Medes and Persians', which could never be changed, is a biblical phrase; the Mede is the lawmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink brewed from fermented honey and water.

clue.text: Top of the column? First class!

definitions.meaning: the carved head of an architectural pillar
an old exclamation meaning excellent or splendid

explanation.definitionFit: In architecture the crowning piece of a pillar has this name, and as an exclamation it once meant splendid or excellent.

clue.text: Also a mathematical exercise with a friend

parts.note: an addition is a sum, a piece of arithmetic
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Besides, a sum done with a pal's help.
explanation.definitionFit: Additionally is an adverb meaning in addition, besides, as well.

clue.text: Who hears may read it

definitions.meaning: a person who pays attention with their ears
a reader of the former BBC weekly magazine of that name

explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a weekly magazine published by the BBC from 1929 to 1991, so the person who hears might also read it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who hears is a hearer by ear; the same name belonged to a BBC weekly magazine that people read.

clue.text: Pope — topping wall-maker

indicators.note: topping means cutting off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the Roman emperor Hadrian built the wall across northern England

explanation.surface: A pontiff executes the builder of a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' removes the first letter H from HADRIAN. Adrian IV was the only English pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Several popes took this name, including Adrian IV, the only Englishman to hold the office.

clue.text: At work on the summit

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Labouring away at the peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop is a preposition meaning on top of, at the highest point.

clue.text: Ground for disturbing Tina when about to go wrong

indicators.note: about means the anagrammed name goes around the other piece
disturbing means the letters of the name are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
to err is to go wrong or make a mistake

explanation.surface: Reasons for upsetting Tina as she is about to make a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' turns TINA into TAIN, and 'about' puts that around ERR: T-ERR-AIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land or ground considered for its physical features.

clue.text: Page taking umbrage at introduction

parts.note: to take umbrage at something is to resent it

explanation.surface: A young servant is offended at being introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenting someone, as at court, is introducing them formally, so the act is an introduction.

clue.text: Growth of suburbia can make a spirit sad

indicators.note: can make tells us the letters of these words can be made into something else

explanation.surface: Life in the suburbs can leave a soul gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges A SPIRIT SAD. 'Growth' looks like spreading suburbs, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The hardy, broad-leaved potted plant was a fixture of suburban front rooms, a byword for middle-class respectability.

clue.text: Descent of an actor

definitions.meaning: lineage, as drawn in a family chart
Sir Herbert Beerbohm ..., the Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager

explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous London actor-manager who founded what became RADA.
explanation.definitionFit: A family chart of ancestry has this name, and it was also the surname of the actor-manager Beerbohm Tree.

clue.text: Genuineness of a new hit tune on Rome, for instance

indicators.note: new means the letters of these words appear in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Rome is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Is a fresh chart-topper set in the Italian capital the real thing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges HIT TUNE as UTHENTI, between A and CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Authenticity is the quality of being real or not counterfeit, the same as genuineness.

clue.text: Steer the little ones back

indicators.note: back means the word for the children is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: tots are small children

explanation.surface: Guide the children home again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TOTS round. A stot is a dialect word, chiefly Scottish and northern English, for a young bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: In dialect a young castrated bullock, a steer, is called a stot.

clue.text: Exclaim at weaving a lace with jute

indicators.note: weaving means the threads of these letters are interlaced into a new order

explanation.surface: Crying out while making lace from jute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaving' rearranges A LACE with JUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage to ejaculate is to utter suddenly, to cry out.

clue.text: Used stucco — made mistake

indicators.note: mistake means the letters of these words are taken wrongly, put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: The plasterer used stucco and got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' rearranges STUCCO and MADE. 'Used' means used to, not employed.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed means habituated, as in being used to something.

clue.text: Read the roll, as umpires do

definitions.meaning: read out a list of names to check who is present
a cricket umpire announces the end of each set of six balls

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the umpire calls 'over' after each set of six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-call of names has this name, and it is also what a cricket umpire does at the end of six balls.

clue.text: Macbeth, say, takes half to the Isle

parts.note: Macbeth was the Thane of Glamis and Cawdor, an example of a thane

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word gives just its first letter

explanation.surface: The Scottish usurper takes over half the island.
explanation.walkthrough: Thanet, in Kent, was once a true island, and is still called the Isle of Thanet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Thanet is the north-eastern corner of Kent, once cut off from the mainland.

clue.text: Man at the Palace — he leaves the messenger outside

indicators.note: outside means the messenger's letters go around the leftover letter

parts.note: a courier is a messenger

indicators.note: he leaves means those two letters walk out of the little word, leaving one

explanation.surface: A royal attendant leaves the messenger standing outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he leaves' takes HE from THE, leaving T, and 'outside' puts COURIER around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier is an attendant at a royal court, a man at the palace.

clue.text: Throw horseman out of Parliament?

definitions.meaning: to throw a rider from the saddle
to remove an MP from their seat

explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge a rider from the saddle, and to remove a Member of Parliament from their seat at an election.

clue.text: Irish boy accepts a degree from an old man of Yemen

indicators.note: accepts means the boy's name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Sean is an Irish boy's name
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: An Irish lad gets a degree from an ancient Arabian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts A and BA inside SEAN. The Sabaeans were the people of Saba, the biblical Sheba, in what is now Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient kingdom of Saba, or Sheba, lay in south-west Arabia, so one of its people was an old inhabitant of Yemen.

clue.text: The height of the French Revolution

definitions.meaning: a great elevation of land, a peak
the radical Jacobin faction seated on the high benches of the Convention

explanation.walkthrough: In the French Revolution the radical deputies sitting on the highest benches were called the Montagne.
explanation.definitionFit: A lofty peak, and the name of the radical group in the National Convention of revolutionary France.

clue.text: A biographer of Mehitabel creates chaos

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article
in Don Marquis's stories, archy the cockroach typed the tales of Mehitabel the alley cat

explanation.surface: A writer's life of his subject creates mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Marquis's archy, a cockroach poet, recorded the doings of Mehitabel the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is lawlessness and disorder, a state of chaos.

clue.text: Way in which best man embraces 10

indicators.note: embraces means the saint's letters wrap around the other piece

parts.note: ST is short for saint, the best kind of man
the answer to 10 across, a family line or the actor

explanation.surface: The groom's supporter hugs a tree at the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts ST around TREE, the answer to 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road, a way through a town.

clue.text: May one arranging figures ban learner returning a list?

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, a ban
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: returning means the list's word is read back to front

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: Could a person handling numbers stop a student handing back a list?
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabulator sets out numbers in columns or tables.

clue.text: A country one organized

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to run something is to organize it

explanation.surface: A nation one person set up.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia.

clue.text: Southend put into ecstasy

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaside town sends people into raptures.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend-on-Sea is an Essex seaside resort, read here as SOUTH and END.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone, in slang, is to thrill or excite them greatly.

clue.text: Blessed worldly legatees

parts.note: the Sermon on the Mount promises that the humble shall inherit the earth, making them blessed heirs of the world

explanation.walkthrough: Matthew 5:5: 'Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.'
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatitudes call the humble blessed and say they will inherit the earth.

clue.text: Figure rice is Clem's ruination

indicators.note: ruination means these words are wrecked and rebuilt in a different order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Rice is what ruined Clem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruination' rearranges RICE, IS and CLEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircle is a geometric figure, half of a round.

clue.text: Hamlet's tribe, note

definitions.note: read as Hamlet is, so it defines what the prince was

parts.note: Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Note the prince's people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet's' reads as 'Hamlet is', and Hamlet was Prince of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's prince is a native of Denmark.

clue.text: Visionary turned out to be right yesterday

indicators.note: turned out means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: The dreamer proved correct about what happened the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges R and YESTERDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry-eyed describes someone idealistic and dreamy, a visionary.
